```python
        ok = np.all([im > 0 for im in imgs.values()], axis=0)
        good_r, good_c = np.where(ok.mean(axis=1) > 0.99)[0], np.where(ok.mean(axis=0) > 0.99)[0]
        if len(good_r) < ok.shape[0] or len(good_c) < ok.shape[1]:
            sl = np.s_[good_r[0]:good_r[-1] + 1, good_c[0]:good_c[-1] + 1]
            print(f"track {int(t)}: cropped to {sl[0].stop - sl[0].start} x {sl[1].stop - sl[1].start} cells with data on every date")
            imgs = {k: v[sl] for k, v in imgs.items()}
        ref = list(g[g.collection == "provisional"].file)
        if not ref:     # a track with no provisional date in this area (162 on 613590): use all its dates
            ref = list(g.file)
            print(f"track {int(t)}: no provisional dates, reference is the mean of all {len(ref)}")
        off, rms = geo.network_offsets(imgs, ref)
        for r in g.itertuples():
            with h5py.File(RS / r.rslc, "r") as h:
                vg = float(np.median(h["geolocationGrid/groundTrackVelocity"][:]))
            drow, dcol = off[r.file]
            ds, da, a, f = radar_offsets(5 * dcol, -5 * drow, l, vg)
            s0 = float(getattr(r, "coreg_slant_m", 0.0) or 0.0)
            a0 = float(getattr(r, "coreg_az_s", 0.0) or 0.0)
            rows.append(dict(file=r.file, date=r.date, track=int(t), collection=r.collection,
                             away_m=round(a, 2), forward_m=round(f, 2),
                             slant_m=round(s0 + ds, 3), az_s=a0 + da, az_m=round((a0 + da) * vg, 2),
                             applied_slant_m=s0, applied_az_s=a0,
                             track_misclosure_rms_m=round(5 * rms, 2)))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df.to_csv(OFFSETS, index=False)
    print(df.to_string(index=False))
    print("wrote", OFFSETS)
    return df


def track_offsets(check="_coreg_k010"):
    """Per-track offset of the co-registered stack against the lidar, from check V3.

    Reads the block shifts of `_nisar_lidar_sim_match_9t.py --stack lidar --kappa 0.1` (the
    lidar simulation with forest echo at 10% of stand height, the best fit on 2026-10-13), takes
    the median over blocks and turns it into slant range and azimuth time. The offsets found
    are added to those the stack already had applied. Split-half check: the median of each
    checkerboard half of the blocks, and how the other half fares after that correction.
    """
    sh = pd.read_csv(RES / f"nisar_lidar_sim_match_shifts{check}_{TAG}.csv")
    sh = sh[sh.block != "tile"].copy()
    sh["half"] = (sh.block.str[1].astype(int) + sh.block.str[2].astype(int)) % 2
    los = json.load(open(RES / f"nisar_los_by_track_{TAG}.json"))
    idx = gfetch.A.usable(pd.read_csv(OUTD / f"nisar_slc_lidar_index_{TAG}.csv"))
    rows = []
    for t, g in sh.groupby("track"):
        if not (idx.track == t).any():
            continue   # no usable (post-June) date on this track, e.g. 613590 track 162
        l = los[str(int(t))]
        away = -np.array([l["east"], l["north"]]) / np.hypot(l["east"], l["north"])
        back = np.array([-away[1], away[0]])          # the check's along_m axis
        a, b = float(g.away_m.median()), float(g.along_m.median())
        e, n = a * away + b * back
        rr = idx[idx.track == t].iloc[0]
        with h5py.File(RS / rr.rslc, "r") as h:
            vg = float(np.median(h["geolocationGrid/groundTrackVelocity"][:]))
        ds, da, _, f = radar_offsets(e, n, l, vg)
        s0 = float(rr.get("track_slant_m", 0.0) or 0.0) if "track_slant_m" in idx else 0.0
        a0 = float(rr.get("track_az_s", 0.0) or 0.0) if "track_az_s" in idx else 0.0
        halves = []
        for k in (0, 1):
            fit, test = g[g.half == k], g[g.half != k]
            ca, cb = fit.away_m.median(), fit.along_m.median()
            halves.append(int((np.hypot(test.away_m - ca, test.along_m - cb) <= 2.5).sum()))
        rows.append(dict(track=int(t), check=check, away_m=round(a, 2), back_m=round(b, 2),
                         slant_m=round(s0 + ds, 3), az_s=a0 + da, az_m=round((a0 + da) * vg, 2),
                         applied_slant_m=s0, applied_az_s=a0,
                         split_half_test_blocks_within_2p5m=f"{halves[0]}/{len(g) - len(g[g.half == 0])}, "
                                                            f"{halves[1]}/{len(g) - len(g[g.half == 1])}"))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df.to_csv(TRACK_OFFSETS, index=False)
    print(df.to_string(index=False))
    print("wrote", TRACK_OFFSETS)
    return df


def pair_coherence(max_days=36):
    """Median 5 x 5 coherence of every same-track pair up to max_days apart, on the stack as it
    is now. Dates that sit metres apart lose coherence; lining them up should bring it back."""
    from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter
    idx = gfetch.A.usable(pd.read_csv(OUTD / f"nisar_slc_lidar_index_{TAG}.csv"))
    state = "co-registered" if "coreg" in idx and idx.coreg.any() else "as placed"
    rows = []
    for t, g in idx.sort_values("date").groupby("track"):
        S = {}
        for r in g.itertuples():
            with rasterio.open(OUTD / r.file) as s:
                S[r.date] = s.read(1)[CORE]
        dates = list(S)
        for i, d1 in enumerate(dates):
            for d2 in dates[i + 1:]:
                days = (pd.Timestamp(d2) - pd.Timestamp(d1)).days
                if days > max_days:
                    continue
                a, b = S[d1], S[d2]
                p = a * np.conj(b)
                num = np.abs(uniform_filter(p.real, 5) + 1j * uniform_filter(p.imag, 5))
                den = np.sqrt(uniform_filter(np.abs(a) ** 2, 5) * uniform_filter(np.abs(b) ** 2, 5))
                rows.append(dict(stack=state, track=int(t), date1=d1, date2=d2, days=days,
                                 coh5_median=round(float(np.median(num / np.maximum(den, 1e-12))), 3)))
    new = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    path = RES / f"nisar_slc_pair_coherence_{TAG}.csv"
    if path.exists():
        old = pd.read_csv(path)
        new = pd.concat([old[old["stack"] != state], new], ignore_index=True)
    new.to_csv(path, index=False)
    print(new[new["stack"] == state].to_string(index=False))
    print("wrote", path)
    return new


def run_v2(block=30):
    """Check V2: is the shift between NASA's placement and ours the one the heights predict?

    Both stacks place the same RSLC samples, so registering them block by block is sharp.
    Predicted shift of NASA's content away from the satellite: (NASA DEM height - lidar height)
    / tan(incidence), averaged over the block. Pass (plan): slope of measured on predicted
    0.9-1.1. Runs on the stack as placed (no co-registration offsets), usable dates only.
    """
    from skimage.registration import phase_cross_correlation
    li = gfetch.A.usable(pd.read_csv(OUTD / f"nisar_slc_lidar_index_{TAG}.csv"))
    if "coreg" in li and li.coreg.any():
        raise SystemExit("V2 needs the stack as placed: rewrite it without --coreg first")
    gi = pd.read_csv(GS / f"nisar_gslc_window_index_{TAG}_5m.csv")
    los = json.load(open(RES / f"nisar_los_by_track_{TAG}.json"))
    X, Y, shape = output_grid(gi.iloc[0])
    lon, lat = geo.utm_to_lonlat(X, Y)
    dh = (geo.dem_heights_isce(NDEM, lon, lat, CONV["dem_half_pixel"])
          - lidar_heights(lon, lat, X, Y)).reshape(shape)[CORE]
    nb = 900 // block
    rows = []
    for t, g in li.groupby("track"):
        l = los[str(int(t))]
        away = -np.array([l["east"], l["north"]]) / np.hypot(l["east"], l["north"])
        tan_i = np.tan(np.radians(l["incidence_deg"]))
        ours = nasa = 0.0
        for r in g.itertuples():
            with rasterio.open(OUTD / r.file) as s:
                ours = ours + np.abs(s.read(1))[CORE].astype(np.float64) ** 2
            gf = gi[(gi.date == r.date) & (gi.track == r.track)].iloc[0].file
            with rasterio.open(GS / gf) as s:
                nasa = nasa + np.abs(s.read(1))[CORE].astype(np.float64) ** 2
        ours, nasa = np.sqrt(ours), np.sqrt(nasa)
        for i in range(nb):
            for j in range(nb):
                sl = np.s_[i * block:(i + 1) * block, j * block:(j + 1) * block]
                s, _, _ = phase_cross_correlation(ours[sl], nasa[sl], upsample_factor=20)
                e, n = -5 * s[1], 5 * s[0]          # where NASA puts the content, against ours
                rows.append(dict(track=int(t), block_row=i, block_col=j,
                                 measured_away_m=round(e * away[0] + n * away[1], 2),
                                 measured_across_m=round(-e * away[1] + n * away[0], 2),
                                 nasa_minus_lidar_height_m=round(float(np.mean(dh[sl])), 2),
                                 predicted_away_m=round(float(np.mean(dh[sl])) / tan_i, 2)))
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df.to_csv(RES / f"nisar_regeocode_v2_blocks_{TAG}.csv", index=False)
    out = []
    for t, g in df.groupby("track"):
        slope, icpt = np.polyfit(g.predicted_away_m, g.measured_away_m, 1)
        out.append(dict(check="V2 shift against height difference", track=int(t), blocks=len(g),
                        block_m=5 * block, slope=round(float(slope), 3), intercept_m=round(float(icpt), 2),
                        r=round(float(np.corrcoef(g.predicted_away_m, g.measured_away_m)[0, 1]), 3),
                        median_measured_m=round(float(g.measured_away_m.median()), 2),
                        median_predicted_m=round(float(g.predicted_away_m.median()), 2),
                        median_across_m=round(float(g.measured_across_m.median()), 2),
                        passed=bool(0.9 <= slope <= 1.1)))
    out = pd.DataFrame(out)
    out.to_csv(RES / f"nisar_regeocode_v2_checks_{TAG}.csv", index=False)
    print(out.to_string(index=False))
    return out


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--heights", default="nisar_dem", choices=["nisar_dem", "lidar"])
    ap.add_argument("--v2", action="store_true", help="check V2 on the stack as placed")
    ap.add_argument("--v1", nargs="+", help="date pairs as d1:d2, e.g. 20260917_t162A:20260929_t162A")
    ap.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="re-place every date (HH and HV) and write the stack")
    ap.add_argument("--coreg", action="store_true", help="with --write: apply the per-date offsets table")
    ap.add_argument("--absolute", action="store_true", help="with --write --coreg: apply the per-track offsets too")
    ap.add_argument("--track-offsets", metavar="CHECK", help="per-track offsets from a V3 run, e.g. _coreg_k010")
    ap.add_argument("--estimate-offsets", action="store_true", help="per-date offsets of the stack on disk")
    ap.add_argument("--coherence", action="store_true", help="pair coherence of the stack on disk")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.write:
        write_stack(a.heights, coreg=a.coreg, absolute=a.absolute)
        return
    if a.track_offsets:
        track_offsets(a.track_offsets)
        return
    if a.estimate_offsets:
        estimate_offsets()
        return
    if a.coherence:
        pair_coherence()
        return
    if a.v2:
        run_v2()
        return
    if a.heights != "nisar_dem":
        raise SystemExit("--v1 compares against NASA and runs on NASA's DEM only")
    rows = run_v1([tuple(p.split(":")) for p in a.v1])
    RES.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    p = RES / f"nisar_regeocode_v1_checks_{TAG}.csv"
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(p, index=False)
    print("wrote", p)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```
### nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_lidar_sim_match_9t.py
```python
"""Stage 0 of nisar/docs/iterations/nisar_regeocode_plan_9t.md: how far off is NASA's GSLC placement over 9t?

Builds a fake radar brightness image from the 1 m lidar bare earth, then slides it over the real
mean HH image to find the shift that lines them up best.

Simulated brightness (area projection, Small 2011):
  * Each 1 m lidar cell is a facet with normal n. l is the unit vector from ground to satellite.
  * Its weight is the facet area seen by the radar: max(n.l, 0) / n_z (n_z turns map area into
    true facet area). A flat cell weighs l_z = cos(incidence).
  * Facets are binned into radar cells: slant range s = -P.l and along-track a = P.v, where v is
    the horizontal unit vector at right angles to the horizontal look. Bin size 3.1 m slant range
    by 4.4 m along track (the RSLC sample spacing).
  * Each bin's summed weight over the flat value is the simulated brightness. Each 1 m cell takes
    its bin's value. Facing slopes come out bright, back slopes dark, layover very bright.
  * Shadow: n.l <= 0. Layover: the slope facing the satellite is steeper than the incidence angle.
    Terrain blocking further away is not traced. At 38-47 degrees incidence it is rare on 9t.

Match: both images go to dB, minus their 250 m running mean, on the 5 m GSLC grid. The 1 m simulation is
shifted at 1 m steps (25 sub-pixel offsets, each block-averaged to 5 m) and every 5 m lag up to
+-30 m is scored by normalized cross-correlation. Done on the whole tile and on 4 x 4 blocks.

Shift sign: (dx, dy) is how far features sit in the radar image from where the lidar says they
are, in metres east and north. "away_m" is that shift along the horizontal direction pointing
away from the satellite. A DEM that is too high under trees pushes features away from it.
"along_m" is the shift at right angles to that, pointing back against the flight direction.

Gate (plan): every block within +-2.5 m means NASA's placement is good enough.

Datum (fixed 2026-10-13): the simulation sits on the lidar's NAD83(2011) grid and the radar on
WGS84 (ITRF2014). On 9t the same point is 0.80 m west and 1.01 m north in the radar grid. Shifts
are reported in the radar's frame: that datum offset, taken at the stack's mean date, is removed.
The best shift is refined below 1 m with a parabola through the peak and its neighbours.

Canopy (--kappa k, added 2026-10-13): forest echo comes partly from inside the canopy. With k > 0
each facet's echo is binned at the slant range of a point k x canopy height (25 m mean) above the ground,
then mapped back to the map the way our ground-height placement does it. Elevated echo then
lands toward the satellite in the simulation as it does in the radar. k = 0 is bare earth.

Dates: NASA granules in _nisar_area.BAD_DATES are left out. --dates provisional or beta keeps
one processing generation only (beta dates sit 3.2 m closer in slant range, see the plan doc).

Run (about 20 minutes, mostly the remote cube read for the first run):
  python nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_lidar_sim_match_9t.py                  # NASA's GSLC
  python nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_lidar_sim_match_9t.py --stack lidar    # our stack
  python nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_lidar_sim_match_9t.py --stack lidar --dates beta
  python nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_lidar_sim_match_9t.py --figure   # figure only
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import rasterio
from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "nisar" / "code"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "notebooks" / "wellsight_v2"))   # _common (shared project code)
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "nisar" / "code" / "s1_build"))
from _common import path_for  # noqa: E402
import _nisar_area as A  # noqa: E402  (--area picks 9t, 613590 or mkf)

DEM = A.lidar("dem")
CHM = A.lidar("chm")
GS = A.GSLC
OUT = A.RESULTS
FIG = OUT / "figures"
LOS_JSON = OUT / f"nisar_los_by_track_{A.TAG}.json"
# --stack lidar: match our lidar-height re-placement (Stage 3) instead of NASA's GSLC (check V3)
STACK = "lidar" if "--stack" in sys.argv and sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--stack") + 1] == "lidar" else "gslc"
DATES = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--dates") + 1] if "--dates" in sys.argv else "all"   # all, provisional, beta
KAPPA = float(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--kappa") + 1]) if "--kappa" in sys.argv else 0.0
SLC_LIDAR = A.NISAR_DERIVED / "nisar_slc_lidar_5m"
_IDX = pd.read_csv(GS / f"nisar_gslc_window_index_{A.TAG}_5m.csv")
# tracks with at least one usable window (all of track 090's McKean windows are empty)
TRACKS = tuple(int(t) for t in sorted(A.usable(_IDX).track.unique()))


def stack_index():
    """Usable dates of the chosen stack and the folder holding them."""
    if STACK == "gslc":
        idx, folder = _IDX, GS
    else:
        idx, folder = pd.read_csv(SLC_LIDAR / f"nisar_slc_lidar_index_{A.TAG}.csv"), SLC_LIDAR
    idx = A.usable(idx)
    return (idx if DATES == "all" else idx[idx.collection == DATES]), folder


def _suffix():
    if STACK == "gslc":
        s = ""
    else:
        idx, _ = stack_index()
        s = ("_coregabs" if "absolute" in idx and idx.absolute.any() else "_coreg")             if "coreg" in idx and idx.coreg.any() else "_lidarslc"
    return s + {"all": "", "provisional": "_prov", "beta": "_beta"}[DATES] + (f"_k{round(KAPPA * 100):03d}" if KAPPA else "")


# --figure --suffix _coreg_k010 redraws a saved run (its suffix says stack, dates and kappa)
SUF = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--suffix") + 1] if "--suffix" in sys.argv else _suffix()
DS_RANGE, DS_AZ = 3.1, 4.4   # RSLC sample spacing, slant range and along track (m)
MAX_LAG = 30                 # m
BG_M = 250
NBLK = 4 if A.TAG == "9t" else None   # set from the area size in main(): blocks of about 1.1 km
GATE_M = 2.5


def grid_point(xc, yc, epsg):
    """(x, y) of a UTM 17 point in the granule's zone, and the turn from that zone's grid to UTM 17's."""
    if epsg == 32617:
        return xc, yc, 0.0
    from pyproj import Transformer
    tr = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:32617", f"EPSG:{epsg}", always_xy=True)
    px, py = tr.transform(xc, yc)
    qx, qy = tr.transform(xc, yc + 1000.0)       # UTM 17 grid north, seen in the other zone
    return px, py, float(np.arctan2(qx - px, qy - py))


def rotate(e, n, rot):
    """East/north components in the granule zone -> UTM 17 grid components."""
    c, s_ = np.cos(rot), np.sin(rot)
    return float(e * c - n * s_), float(e * s_ + n * c)


def read_los():
    """Look vector and incidence per track at the area centre, from one GSLC's radarGrid cubes."""
    try:
        out = {int(k): v for k, v in json.load(open(LOS_JSON)).items()} if LOS_JSON.exists() else {}
    except json.JSONDecodeError:   # a run that died mid-write; read the cubes again
        out = {}
    if all(t in out for t in TRACKS):
        return out
    import h5py, fsspec  # noqa: E401
    from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator
    import _fetch_nisar_gslc_window_9t as fetch
    idx = pd.read_csv(GS / f"nisar_gslc_window_index_{A.TAG}_5m.csv")
    q = fetch.query().set_index("granule")
    if A.TAG == "9t":
        xc, yc, hc = 621750.0, 4595250.0, 380.0   # 9t centre, a typical ellipsoid height
    else:
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = A.bounds("EPSG:32617")
        with rasterio.open(DEM) as s:
            z = s.read(1, out_shape=(200, 200), masked=True)
        # DEM heights are NAVD88; the geoid is about 34 m below the ellipsoid here
        xc, yc, hc = (x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2, float(np.ma.median(z)) - 34.0
    for t in [t for t in TRACKS if t not in out]:
        g = idx[idx.track == t].iloc[-1].granule
        f = fsspec.filesystem("http").open(fetch.signed_url(q.loc[g, "url"]), block_size=8 * 2**20,
                                           cache_type="blockcache")
        with h5py.File(f, "r") as h:
            rg = h["science/LSAR/GSLC/metadata/radarGrid"]
            x, y, z = rg["xCoordinates"][:], rg["yCoordinates"][:], rg["heightAboveEllipsoid"][:]
            epsg = int(h["science/LSAR/GSLC/grids/frequencyA/projection"][()])
            # McKean track 098 comes in UTM 18: look up the centre in that zone, then turn its
            # vectors by the angle between the two zones' grid north (about 4 deg there)
            px, py, rot = grid_point(xc, yc, epsg)
            # read only the 2 x 2 cube cells around the 9t centre (a full cube takes minutes remotely)
            i0 = int(np.clip(np.searchsorted(x, px) - 1, 0, len(x) - 2))
            yi = np.argsort(y)
            j = int(np.clip(np.searchsorted(y[yi], py) - 1, 0, len(y) - 2))
            j0, j1 = sorted((yi[j], yi[j + 1]))
            v = {}
            for k in ("losUnitVectorX", "losUnitVectorY", "alongTrackUnitVectorX",
                      "alongTrackUnitVectorY", "incidenceAngle"):
                a = rg[k][:, j0:j1 + 1, i0:i0 + 2]          # (height, y, x)
                ys = y[j0:j1 + 1]
                if ys[0] > ys[-1]:
                    ys, a = ys[::-1], a[:, ::-1, :]
                v[k] = float(RegularGridInterpolator((z, ys, x[i0:i0 + 2]), a)((hc, py, px)))
        e, n = rotate(v["losUnitVectorX"], v["losUnitVectorY"], rot)
        v["alongTrackUnitVectorX"], v["alongTrackUnitVectorY"] = rotate(
            v["alongTrackUnitVectorX"], v["alongTrackUnitVectorY"], rot)
        out[t] = dict(granule=g, east=e, north=n, up=float(np.sqrt(1 - e * e - n * n)),
                      incidence_deg=v["incidenceAngle"],
                      along_east=v["alongTrackUnitVectorX"], along_north=v["alongTrackUnitVectorY"])
        print(t, out[t])
        json.dump(out, open(LOS_JSON, "w"), indent=2)
    return out


def simulate(dem, l, chm=None, kappa=0.0):
    """Area-projection brightness (ratio to flat ground) per 1 m cell, plus shadow/layover masks.
    kappa > 0: each facet's echo sits kappa x canopy height above the ground (see the docstring)."""
    gy, gx = np.gradient(np.where(np.isfinite(dem), dem, np.nan))   # rows run south: gy is -dz/dnorth
    dzdx, dzdn = gx, -gy
    nz = 1 / np.sqrt(1 + dzdx ** 2 + dzdn ** 2)
    n = np.stack([-dzdx * nz, -dzdn * nz, nz])
    lv = np.array([l["east"], l["north"], l["up"]])
    cos_loc = np.tensordot(lv, n, 1)
    w = np.clip(cos_loc, 0, None) / nz
    shadow = cos_loc <= 0
    lh = np.hypot(lv[0], lv[1])
    away = -lv[:2] / lh                                   # horizontal, away from the satellite
    foreslope = -(dzdx * away[0] + dzdn * away[1])        # rise toward the satellite
    layover = foreslope > np.tan(np.radians(l["incidence_deg"]))
    rr, cc = np.mgrid[0:dem.shape[0], 0:dem.shape[1]]
    e, nn = cc + 0.5, -(rr + 0.5)
    s = -(e * lv[0] + nn * lv[1] + np.nan_to_num(dem) * lv[2])            # ground, as we place pixels
    if kappa:   # a stand echoes as a whole: canopy height averaged over 25 m, not crown by crown
        c = np.where(np.isfinite(chm), chm, 0.0)
        c = uniform_filter(c, 25) / np.maximum(uniform_filter(np.isfinite(chm).astype(float), 25), 1e-6)
    s_echo = s - kappa * c * lv[2] if kappa else s                        # where the echo really is
    vdir = np.array([l["along_east"], l["along_north"]])
    vdir = vdir / np.hypot(*vdir)
    a = e * vdir[0] + nn * vdir[1]
    s0 = min(np.nanmin(s), np.nanmin(s_echo))
    si = np.floor((s - s0) / DS_RANGE).astype(np.int64)
    se = np.floor((s_echo - s0) / DS_RANGE).astype(np.int64)
    ai = np.floor((a - a.min()) / DS_AZ).astype(np.int64)
    key = si * (ai.max() + 1) + ai
    key_echo = se * (ai.max() + 1) + ai
    ok = np.isfinite(dem) & np.isfinite(w)
    tot = np.bincount(key_echo[ok], weights=w[ok], minlength=max(key.max(), key_echo.max()) + 1)
    # flat ground: a bin covers DS_RANGE / sin(inc) of ground range, each m2 weighing l_z
    flat = DS_RANGE / lh * DS_AZ * lv[2]
    sim = tot[key] / flat
    sim[~ok] = np.nan
    return sim.astype(np.float32), shadow & ok, layover & ok


def to_db_hp(a, px):
    """dB minus the 250 m running mean (NaN-aware)."""
    db = 10 * np.log10(np.clip(a, 1e-6, None)) if px != "db" else a
    m = np.isfinite(db)
    k = BG_M // 5 + 1
    bg = uniform_filter(np.where(m, db, 0), k) / np.maximum(uniform_filter(m.astype(float), k), 1e-6)
    return np.where(m, db - bg, np.nan)


def block5(a):
    h, w = a.shape[0] // 5, a.shape[1] // 5
    return np.nanmean(a[:h * 5, :w * 5].reshape(h, 5, w, 5), axis=(1, 3))


def ncc(A, B, lag5, n5):
    """Normalized cross-correlation of A against B shifted by every 5 m lag.

    A and B are padded by lag5. Sums are taken once per lag over the core, then split into
    NBLK x NBLK blocks by reshaping; the tile score adds the block sums."""
    bs = n5 // NBLK
    core = (slice(lag5, lag5 + bs * NBLK),) * 2
    Ac = A[core]
    out = {}
    def bsum(x):
        return x.reshape(NBLK, bs, NBLK, bs).sum(axis=(1, 3))
    for dy in range(-lag5, lag5 + 1):
        for dx in range(-lag5, lag5 + 1):
            Bc = np.roll(B, (dy, dx), axis=(0, 1))[core]
            m = np.isfinite(Ac) & np.isfinite(Bc)
            a, b = np.where(m, Ac, 0), np.where(m, Bc, 0)
            S = [bsum(v) for v in (m.astype(float), a, b, a * b, a * a, b * b)]
            for name, idx in [("tile", (slice(None), slice(None)))] +                     [(f"b{i}{j}", (i, j)) for i in range(NBLK) for j in range(NBLK)]:
                N, sa, sb, sab, saa, sbb = (np.sum(v[idx]) for v in S)
                if N < 500:
                    continue
                cov = sab - sa * sb / N
                den = np.sqrt((saa - sa * sa / N) * (sbb - sb * sb / N))
                out.setdefault(name, {})[(dy, dx)] = float(cov / den)
    return out


# lost/found palette reused (CLAUDE.md): dataviz validator --pairs all, worst pair dE 21.1 deutan,
# 22.6 normal, all >= 3:1 on white. Tracks also differ by marker shape.
# Track 098 (McKean only) adds teal #00909A: dataviz validate_palette.js --mode light --pairs all
# on all four (2026-10-12), ALL CHECKS PASS, worst pair #00909A-#1F5FA8 dE 15.1 deutan, 15.2 normal.
TRACK98_C = "#00909A"
TRACK_STYLE = {26: ("#1F5FA8", "o", "track 026 (descending, looks east)"),
               90: ("#D97706", "s", "track 090 (ascending, looks west)"),
               162: ("#A31515", "^", "track 162 (ascending, looks west)"),
               98: (TRACK98_C, "D", "track 098 (descending, looks east)")}
ARROW_X = 25   # arrows drawn 25 times longer than the shift


def mean_hh_db(t):
    """Mean HH power in dB over the chosen dates of track t, from NASA's stack or from ours.
    (Before 2026-10-13 NASA's stack used the bright-target layer: all dates, bad ones too.)"""
    idx, folder = stack_index()
    idx = idx[idx.track == t]
    acc = None
    for f in idx.file:
        with rasterio.open(folder / f) as s:
            p = np.abs(s.read(1)).astype(np.float64) ** 2
        acc = p if acc is None else acc + p
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        return (10 * np.log10(acc / len(idx))).astype(np.float32)


def datum_offset():
    """Where the radar grid (WGS84 = ITRF2014) puts the area centre minus where the lidar grid
    (NAD83(2011)) puts it, east and north metres, at the mean date of the stack."""
    from pyproj import Transformer
    idx, _ = stack_index()
    d = pd.to_datetime(idx.date)
    epoch = float(np.mean(d.dt.year + (d.dt.dayofyear - 0.5) / 365.25))
    with rasterio.open(DEM) as s:
        crs, b = s.crs, s.bounds
    xc, yc = (b.left + b.right) / 2, (b.bottom + b.top) / 2
    lon, lat = Transformer.from_crs(crs, "EPSG:6318", always_xy=True).transform(xc, yc)
    # PROJ's NAD83(2011) -> "WGS 84" is a null transform; ITRF2014 (EPSG:7912) stands in
    lo, la, _, _ = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:6319", "EPSG:7912", always_xy=True).transform(lon, lat, 0.0, epoch)
    xi, yi = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:4326", "EPSG:32617", always_xy=True).transform(lo, la)
    return float(xi - xc), float(yi - yc), round(epoch, 2)


def refine(sc, dx, dy):
    """Sub-metre peak: a parabola through the best 1 m shift and its two neighbours, per axis."""
    def vertex(m, c, p):
        den = m - 2 * c + p
        return 0.5 * (m - p) / den if np.isfinite(den) and den < 0 else 0.0
    c = sc[(dx, dy)]
    ox = vertex(sc.get((dx - 1, dy), np.nan), c, sc.get((dx + 1, dy), np.nan))
    oy = vertex(sc.get((dx, dy - 1), np.nan), c, sc.get((dx, dy + 1), np.nan))
    return dx + float(np.clip(ox, -0.5, 0.5)), dy + float(np.clip(oy, -0.5, 0.5))


def figure():
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    df = pd.read_csv(OUT / f"nisar_lidar_sim_match_shifts{SUF}_{A.TAG}.csv")
    nblk = int(df.block[df.block != "tile"].str[1].astype(int).max()) + 1
    blk = df[df.block != "tile"]
    with rasterio.open(A.lidar("hillshade")) as s:
        hs = s.read(1, out_shape=(900, 900)).astype(float)
        b = s.bounds
    bs = (b.right - b.left) / nblk
    nt = len(TRACKS)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, nt + 1, figsize=(4.25 * (nt + 1), 4.6), gridspec_kw=dict(width_ratios=[1] * nt + [1.15]))
    for k, t in enumerate(TRACKS):
        a = ax[k]
        a.imshow(hs, cmap="gray", extent=(b.left, b.right, b.bottom, b.top), alpha=0.8)
        col, mk, lab = TRACK_STYLE[t]
        for _, r in blk[blk.track == t].iterrows():
            i, j = int(r.block[1]), int(r.block[2])
            xc, yc = b.left + (j + 0.5) * bs, b.top - (i + 0.5) * bs
            a.annotate("", xy=(xc + ARROW_X * r.dx_east_m, yc + ARROW_X * r.dy_north_m), xytext=(xc, yc),
                       arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=col, lw=2))
            a.plot(xc, yc, mk, color=col, ms=5)
            a.text(xc, yc - 0.32 * bs, f"{np.hypot(r.dx_east_m, r.dy_north_m):.0f} m", ha="center",
                   fontsize=7, color="black", bbox=dict(fc="white", ec="none", alpha=0.7, pad=0.5))
        a.set_title(lab, fontsize=9)
        a.set_xticks([]); a.set_yticks([])
    fig.text(0.01, 0.012, f"Arrow = where the radar puts features relative to the lidar ground, drawn {ARROW_X} "
             "times longer. Label = length of the shift.", fontsize=7)
    a = ax[nt]
    for t in TRACKS:
        col, mk, lab = TRACK_STYLE[t]
        g = blk[blk.track == t]
        a.scatter(g.canopy_h_mean_m, g.away_m, color=col, marker=mk, s=36, label=lab.split(" (")[0],
                  edgecolor="white", linewidth=0.8)
    a.axhspan(-GATE_M, GATE_M, color="#8E959B", alpha=0.25, lw=0)
    a.text(0.02, GATE_M - 0.15, "gate: within 2.5 m", fontsize=7, va="top", transform=a.get_yaxis_transform())
    a.set_xlabel("mean canopy height in block (m, lidar)")
    a.set_ylabel("shift away from the satellite (m)")
    a.set_title("Shift against canopy height", fontsize=9)
    a.legend(fontsize=7, frameon=False)
    a.grid(alpha=0.3)
    import re
    stack = {"": "NASA's GSLC", "_lidarslc": "our lidar-height placement",
             "_coreg": "our placement, dates lined up",
             "_coregabs": "our placement, dates lined up and each track tied to the lidar"}[
        re.sub(r"_prov|_beta|_k\d{3}", "", SUF)]
    k = re.search(r"_k(\d{3})", SUF)
    sim = f"forest echo at {int(k.group(1))}% of stand height" if k else "bare earth"
    dates = ", provisional dates only" if "_prov" in SUF else ", beta dates only" if "_beta" in SUF else ""
    fig.suptitle(f"NISAR over {A.TAG}: {stack}{dates}, against a lidar radar simulation ({sim}). {nblk} x {nblk} blocks of about 1.1 km",
                 fontsize=10)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.04, 1, 1))
    FIG.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    path = FIG / f"nisar_lidar_sim_match{SUF}_{A.TAG}.png"
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150)
    print("wrote", path)


def main():
    global NBLK
    los = read_los()
    de, dn, epoch = datum_offset()
    print(f"datum: radar grid minus lidar grid = {de:+.2f} m east, {dn:+.2f} m north at {epoch}")
    with rasterio.open(DEM) as s:
        dem = s.read(1).astype(np.float64)
        dem[dem == s.nodata] = np.nan
        dtf = s.transform
    with rasterio.open(CHM) as s:
        chm = s.read(1).astype(np.float32)
        chm[(chm == s.nodata) | (chm < 0)] = np.nan
    # the 5 m GSLC grid: DEM cell (0,0) is at 619500, 4597500; GSLC edge at 619295, 4597705
    with rasterio.open(GS / f"nisar_bright_targets_layers_t{TRACKS[-1]:03d}_{A.TAG}.tif") as s:
        gtf, gshape = s.transform, s.shape
    assert dem.shape[0] == dem.shape[1], "the block layout assumes a square lidar area"
    c0 = int(round((dtf.c - gtf.c) / 5))
    r0 = int(round((gtf.f - dtf.f) / 5))
    n5 = dem.shape[0] // 5
    if NBLK is None:
        NBLK = max(1, round(n5 * 5 / 1125))
    lag5 = MAX_LAG // 5
    rows, sims = [], {}
    chm5 = block5(np.where(np.isfinite(chm), chm, np.nan))
    for t in TRACKS:
        l = los[t]
        sim, shadow, layover = simulate(dem, l, chm, KAPPA)
        sims[t] = (sim, shadow, layover)
        hh = mean_hh_db(t)
        # radar image cut to the lidar footprint, with a lag margin
        R = to_db_hp(hh, "db")
        Rc = R[r0 - lag5:r0 + n5 + lag5, c0 - lag5:c0 + n5 + lag5]
        away = -np.array([l["east"], l["north"]]) / np.hypot(l["east"], l["north"])
        bs = n5 // NBLK
        blocks = [("tile", slice(lag5, lag5 + bs * NBLK), slice(lag5, lag5 + bs * NBLK))]
        for i in range(NBLK):
            for j in range(NBLK):
                blocks.append((f"b{i}{j}", slice(lag5 + i * bs, lag5 + (i + 1) * bs),
                               slice(lag5 + j * bs, lag5 + (j + 1) * bs)))
        scores = {b[0]: {} for b in blocks}
        for oy in range(5):
            for ox in range(5):
                # shift the 1 m sim by (ox east, oy south) m, then block to 5 m
                sh = np.full_like(sim, np.nan)
                sh[oy:, ox:] = sim[:sim.shape[0] - oy, :sim.shape[1] - ox]
                S = to_db_hp(block5(sh), "lin")
                Sp = np.full_like(Rc, np.nan)
                Sp[lag5:lag5 + n5, lag5:lag5 + n5] = S[:n5, :n5]
                for name, sc in ncc(Rc, Sp, lag5, n5).items():
                    for (dy, dx), v in sc.items():
                        # total shift of sim content: east = 5*dx + ox, south = 5*dy + oy
                        scores[name][(5 * dx + ox, -(5 * dy + oy))] = v
        for name, ry, rx in blocks:
            sc = scores[name]
            if not sc:   # block outside the lidar (42% of the McKean box has none)
                continue
            (ix, iy), best = max(sc.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
            fx, fy = refine(sc, ix, iy)
            # in the radar's frame: take off the NAD83 -> ITRF offset of the simulation's grid
            dx_m, dy_m = round(fx - de, 1), round(fy - dn, 1)
            zero = sc.get((0, 0), np.nan)
            sub = (slice(ry.start - lag5, ry.stop - lag5), slice(rx.start - lag5, rx.stop - lag5))
            rows.append(dict(track=t, block=name, dx_east_m=dx_m, dy_north_m=dy_m,
                             away_m=round(dx_m * away[0] + dy_m * away[1], 1),
                             along_m=round(-dx_m * away[1] + dy_m * away[0], 1),
                             ncc_best=round(best, 3), ncc_zero_shift=round(zero, 3),
                             canopy_h_mean_m=round(float(np.nanmean(chm5[sub])), 1),
                             canopy_cover=round(float(np.nanmean(chm5[sub] > 2)), 2),
                             at_lag_edge=bool(max(abs(ix), abs(iy)) >= MAX_LAG)))
        print(pd.DataFrame([r for r in rows if r["track"] == t]).to_string())

    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    df.to_csv(OUT / f"nisar_lidar_sim_match_shifts{SUF}_{A.TAG}.csv", index=False)

    # sim rasters on the 5 m GSLC grid (gitignored folder; small). They do not depend on the
    # stack, so only the NASA all-dates run writes them (parallel runs would collide).
    for t, (sim, shadow, layover) in (sims.items() if STACK == "gslc" and DATES == "all" else []):
        bands = {"sim_brightness_db": 10 * np.log10(np.clip(block5(sim), 1e-6, None)),
                 "shadow_fraction": block5(shadow.astype(np.float32)),
                 "layover_fraction": block5(layover.astype(np.float32))}
        path = GS / f"nisar_lidar_sim_t{t:03d}_{A.TAG}.tif"
        with rasterio.open(path, "w", driver="GTiff", height=gshape[0], width=gshape[1], count=3,
                           dtype="float32", crs="EPSG:32617", transform=gtf, nodata=np.nan,
                           compress="deflate") as dst:
            for i, (k, a) in enumerate(bands.items(), 1):
                full = np.full(gshape, np.nan, np.float32)
                full[r0:r0 + n5, c0:c0 + n5] = a[:n5, :n5]
                dst.write(full, i)
                dst.set_band_description(i, k)
        print("wrote", path)

    blk = df[df.block != "tile"]
    idx, _ = stack_index()
    summ = dict(params=dict(range_bin_m=DS_RANGE, az_bin_m=DS_AZ, max_lag_m=MAX_LAG, bg_m=BG_M,
                            blocks=f"{NBLK}x{NBLK}", gate_m=GATE_M, radar_image="mean HH power in dB",
                            stack=STACK + SUF.replace("_prov", "").replace("_beta", ""), dates=DATES,
                            dates_per_track={int(k): int(v) for k, v in idx.groupby("track").size().items()},
                            left_out=sorted(f"{d} t{t:03d}" for d, t in A.BAD_DATES),
                            datum_offset_removed_east_north_m=[round(de, 2), round(dn, 2)], datum_epoch=epoch,
                            peak="1 m search, parabola refined", kappa=KAPPA),
                los=los,
                block_median_m={int(t): dict(away=round(float(g.away_m.median()), 2), along=round(float(g.along_m.median()), 2),
                                             total=round(float(np.hypot(g.dx_east_m, g.dy_north_m).median()), 2))
                                for t, g in df[df.block != "tile"].groupby("track")},
                tile=df[df.block == "tile"].set_index("track")[["dx_east_m", "dy_north_m", "away_m",
                                                                 "ncc_best", "ncc_zero_shift"]].to_dict("index"),
                blocks_within_gate=int((np.hypot(blk.dx_east_m, blk.dy_north_m) <= GATE_M).sum()),
                blocks_total=int(len(blk)),
                corr_away_vs_canopy_by_track={int(t): round(float(np.corrcoef(g.away_m, g.canopy_h_mean_m)[0, 1]), 2)
                                              for t, g in blk.groupby("track")})
    json.dump(summ, open(OUT / f"nisar_lidar_sim_match_summary{SUF}_{A.TAG}.json", "w"), indent=2, default=int)
    print(json.dumps(summ, indent=2, default=int))
    figure()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    figure() if "--figure" in sys.argv else main()

```
### nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_gslc_stack_pad_pit_seasonal_9t.py
```python
"""Multi-date NISAR GSLC brightness over 9t: pads and pits against their surroundings, by season.

WHY
---
One January GCOV image showed a faint pad signal: open pads about 0.8 dB darker
in HH than the forest ring (`nisar/docs/iterations/nisar_gcov_pad_vs_forest_backscatter_9t.md`).
A single image is grainy, so that signal could not be read pad by pad.
Averaging many dates suppresses the grain. The GSLC is also posted at 5 m instead
of 10 m. This script asks three questions:

  1. With the grain averaged down, do pads differ from their surroundings?
  2. Does the leaf-on against leaf-off change differ? That ratio is taken within
     one track, so terrain and viewing geometry cancel.
  3. Does anything show at pit scale?

DATA
----
Windows written by `nisar/code/s1_build/_fetch_nisar_gslc_window_9t.py`
to `nisar/derived/9t/nisar_gslc_5m/`, plus its index CSV. Complex HH and HV at a
5 m posting, EPSG:32617. There are three tracks: 090 ascending, 162 ascending and
026 descending. Windows with under half their pixels valid are dropped;
2026-07-22 track 026D has none.

Seasons:
  * leaf-off fall: 2026-10-21 .. 2026-11-30 (standard collection; after leaf drop in western PA)
  Since 2026-11-19 amplitude uses June 2026 onward only (user decision). The beta fall 2025 and
  winter windows were dropped on 2026-11-20. Early October 2026 (leaves turning) is in neither season.
  * leaf-on:       2026-06-01 .. 2026-09-30 (provisional collection)

The beta and provisional collections were processed by different software
versions. A calibration offset between them would move every pixel by the same
amount. Feature-minus-ring differences cancel such an offset.

METHOD
------
  * Intensity is |s|^2. It is averaged per track and season in linear power.
  * The seasonal change for a set of pixels is a ratio of means:
    mean(leaf-on) / mean(leaf-off fall), in dB. It is not a mean of per-pixel
    ratios, which are far more skewed.
  * Pads: core pixels have their centre at least 3 m inside the pad. The ring is
    20-60 m outside, kept 10 m clear of every pad and road.
  * Pits: `pit_outside` polygons, meaning the whole pit including its rim. The
    ring is 10-30 m outside, kept 5 m clear of every pit and road.
  * **Decoy null (the key control).** Radar brightness is right-skewed. The mean
    of a few pixels therefore sits below the mean of many, even over identical
    ground. A pit covers about 8 pixels and its ring hundreds. A trial run
    without this control showed pits "2.4 dB darker" in seasonal change, while
    open and closed canopy did not differ at all pixel by pixel. That was the
    size effect.
    Each feature therefore gets 5 decoys: the same shape moved 150-600 m in a
    random direction, onto background at least 20 m from any pad, pit or road.
    Each decoy gets a ring built the same way. The excess is the feature's
    difference minus the median of its decoys' differences. Only the excess is
    evidence of a real signal.
  * Positive control, per pixel (so no size effect): background pixels under
    10% canopy against pixels over 90%, from the 2019 lidar CHM.
  * Registration, per track: the leaf-on HV mean is correlated with canopy cover
    at shifts of -20..+20 m. A shift is applied only when the best correlation
    is at least 0.10, the peak is inside the search range, and it beats the
    unshifted correlation by at least 0.02. Otherwise the track is used as
    delivered. The GCOV test measured about 10 m of offset on the beta data. At
    5 m pixels an offset that size smears a pit into its ring.
  * Each track's value is computed separately and then averaged over tracks.
    Tests are the Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the excess and the AUC of
    feature differences against all decoy differences. 95% CI by bootstrapping
    features.

Run:
  python nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_gslc_stack_pad_pit_seasonal_9t.py
  python nisar/code/s5_eval/_nisar_gslc_stack_pad_pit_seasonal_9t.py --force-best-shift

--force-best-shift applies each track's best canopy-correlation shift whatever its
strength. It is a sensitivity run. Its outputs carry `_forcedshift` in the name.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import rasterio
from rasterio.features import rasterize
from rasterio.warp import Resampling, reproject
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu, spearmanr, wilcoxon
from shapely.affinity import translate

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "nisar" / "code"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "notebooks" / "wellsight_v2"))   # _common (shared project code)
from _common import path_for, read_layer  # noqa: E402
import _nisar_area as A  # noqa: E402  (--area picks 9t, 613590 or mkf)

SRC = A.GSLC
INDEX = A.INDEX
ANN = path_for("truth") / "annotations_proj.gpkg"
CHM = A.lidar("chm")
OUT = A.RESULTS
FIG = OUT / "figures"
CRS = "EPSG:32617"

SEASONS = {"leafoff_fall": ("2026-10-21", "2026-11-30"),
           "leafon": ("2026-06-01", "2026-09-30")}
PAD_CORE_M, PAD_RING, PAD_EXCL = 3.0, (20.0, 60.0), 10.0
PIT_RING, PIT_EXCL = (10.0, 30.0), 5.0
DECOY_R = (150.0, 600.0)   # control-spot distance range, m
SHIFTS = range(-20, 21, 5)
REG_MIN_RHO = 0.10   # below this the canopy correlation is too weak to locate a shift
N_PLACEBO = 5
B, SEED = 2000, 20260930

# lost/found pair, validate_palette.py --mode light --pairs all "#1F5FA8,#D97706":
# worst pair dE 21.1 deutan, 22.6 normal. Maps: greyscale, and PuOr (purple-orange,
# no green) for the signed seasonal change. Features and decoys also differ by marker.
FEAT_C, RING_C, INK = "#1F5FA8", "#D97706", "#141A1F"


def db(x):
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        return 10.0 * np.log10(x)


def load_stack():
    idx = pd.read_csv(INDEX)
    keep = A.usable_stack(idx)
    for f in idx.loc[~idx.file.isin(keep.file), "file"]:
        print(f"dropping {f}: valid fraction below 0.5 or a bad granule")
    idx = keep.reset_index(drop=True)
    grids, bounds = set(), []
    for f in idx.file:
        with rasterio.open(SRC / f) as r:
            grids.add((r.transform.c % 5, r.transform.f % 5))
            bounds.append(r.bounds)
    if len(grids) != 1:
        raise RuntimeError(f"windows are not on one 5 m lattice: {grids}")
    x0 = max(b.left for b in bounds); x1 = min(b.right for b in bounds)
    y0 = max(b.bottom for b in bounds); y1 = min(b.top for b in bounds)
    tf = rasterio.Affine(5.0, 0, x0, 0, -5.0, y1)
    shape = (int(round((y1 - y0) / 5)), int(round((x1 - x0) / 5)))
    inten = {}
    for row in idx.itertuples():
        with rasterio.open(SRC / row.file) as r:
            a = r.read(window=rasterio.windows.from_bounds(x0, y0, x1, y1, r.transform))
        # the writer holds 0 where the swath does not reach (NASA's convention); that is "no sample", not
        # zero power, so it becomes NaN here and never enters a mean
        valid = (a != 0) & np.isfinite(a)
        inten[row.file] = tuple(np.where(valid[i], np.abs(a[i]) ** 2, np.nan) for i in (0, 1))
        assert inten[row.file][0].shape == shape, (row.file, inten[row.file][0].shape, shape)
    return idx, inten, tf, shape


# Short raster names: polarization, season, track. Values are season-mean dB, as delivered
# (no shift to the lidar); the change raster is summer mean minus fall mean, in dB.
RASTER_METRIC_NAME = {"leafoff_fall": "fall_2026",
                      "leafon": "summer_2026", "change_leafon_vs_fall": "change_summer_minus_fall"}


def raster_name(metric: str, track: int, direction: str, tag: str) -> str:
    """metric is '<pol>_<season key>', e.g. 'hv_leafon'. Only as-delivered rasters are written."""
    assert tag == "asdelivered", tag
    pol, key = metric.split("_", 1)
    return f"nisar_{pol}_{RASTER_METRIC_NAME[key]}_track{track:03d}_{A.TAG}_5m.tif"


def season_of(d: str):
    for s, (a, b) in SEASONS.items():
        if a <= d <= b:
            return s
    return None


def canopy_cover(tf, shape, shift=(0.0, 0.0)):
    """Share of 1 m CHM cells above 2 m in each 5 m pixel (2019 lidar)."""
    with rasterio.open(CHM) as r:
        chm = r.read(1, masked=True)
        src = np.where(chm.mask, np.nan, (chm.filled(0) > 2.0).astype(np.float32))
        dst = np.full(shape, np.nan, np.float32)
        t = rasterio.Affine(tf.a, 0, tf.c + shift[0], 0, tf.e, tf.f + shift[1])
        reproject(src, dst, src_transform=r.transform, src_crs=r.crs, src_nodata=np.nan,
                  dst_transform=t, dst_crs=CRS, dst_nodata=np.nan, resampling=Resampling.average)
    return dst


def auc(a, b):
    a, b = np.asarray(a), np.asarray(b)
    return float(mannwhitneyu(a, b).statistic / (len(a) * len(b))) if len(a) and len(b) else np.nan


def pixel_index(geom, tf, shape):
    """Flat indices of pixels whose centre lies in geom; rasterized on a small window."""
    if geom.is_empty:
        return np.array([], dtype=np.int64)
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = geom.bounds
    c0 = max(0, int(np.floor((x0 - tf.c) / tf.a)))
    c1 = min(shape[1], int(np.ceil((x1 - tf.c) / tf.a)) + 1)
    r0 = max(0, int(np.floor((y1 - tf.f) / tf.e)))
    r1 = min(shape[0], int(np.ceil((y0 - tf.f) / tf.e)) + 1)
    if c1 <= c0 or r1 <= r0:
        return np.array([], dtype=np.int64)
    wtf = rasterio.Affine(tf.a, 0, tf.c + c0 * tf.a, 0, tf.e, tf.f + r0 * tf.e)
    m = rasterize([(geom, 1)], out_shape=(r1 - r0, c1 - c0), transform=wtf, fill=0, dtype="uint8")
    rr, cc = np.nonzero(m)
    return (rr + r0) * shape[1] + (cc + c0)


def ring_geom(g, ring, excl):
    return g.buffer(ring[1]).difference(g.buffer(ring[0])).difference(excl)


def pixel_sets(geom, core_m, ring, excl, tf, shape, ok_flat):
    core = pixel_index(geom.buffer(-core_m) if core_m else geom, tf, shape)
    rg = pixel_index(ring_geom(geom, ring, excl), tf, shape)
    return core[ok_flat[core]], rg[ok_flat[rg]]


def placebo_sets(geom, core_m, ring, excl, tf, shape, ok_flat, bg_flat, rng, k, tries=60):
    """Up to k copies of geom moved 150-600 m onto background, each with its own ring."""
    out = []
    for _ in range(tries):
        if len(out) == k:
            break
        a, r = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi), rng.uniform(*DECOY_R)
        g = translate(geom, r * np.cos(a), r * np.sin(a))
        core = pixel_index(g.buffer(-core_m) if core_m else g, tf, shape)
        if len(core) == 0 or not bg_flat[core].all():
            continue
        rg = pixel_index(ring_geom(g, ring, excl), tf, shape)
        rg = rg[ok_flat[rg]]
        if len(rg) < 10:
            continue
        out.append((core, rg))
    return out


def set_value(core, rg, L, num, den):
    """Feature-minus-ring in dB for one track. With den, a ratio of means (seasonal change)."""
    def m(idx, k):
        v = L[k][idx]
        v = v[np.isfinite(v)]
        return v.mean() if len(v) else np.nan
    if num not in L or (den and den not in L):
        return np.nan
    f = db(m(core, num)) - (db(m(core, den)) if den else 0.0)
    r = db(m(rg, num)) - (db(m(rg, den)) if den else 0.0)
    return f - r


N_PERM = 5000


def swap_test(mat, rng):
    """Swap test over features. mat is (feature, 1 + decoys): column 0 the feature, the rest its decoys.

    Null: a feature is no different from its decoys, so any of its series could be "the feature".
    Each permutation picks one series per feature and scores it against the median of the others;
    the statistic is the median over features. Returns observed, p (two-sided), null 95% bounds.
    """
    d_by_f = []
    for row in mat:
        r = np.asarray(row, float)
        ok = np.isfinite(r)
        if not ok[0] or ok.sum() < 3:
            continue
        v = r[ok]
        d = np.array([v[j] - np.median(np.delete(v, j)) for j in range(len(v))])
        d_by_f.append(d)
    if len(d_by_f) < 10:
        return None
    obs = float(np.median([d[0] for d in d_by_f]))
    picks = np.column_stack([d[rng.integers(0, len(d), N_PERM)] for d in d_by_f])
    null = np.median(picks, axis=1)
    return dict(n=len(d_by_f), observed=obs,
                p_two_sided=float((1 + (np.abs(null) >= abs(obs)).sum()) / (1 + N_PERM)),
                null_lo=float(np.percentile(null, 2.5)), null_hi=float(np.percentile(null, 97.5)))


def main() -> int:
    import argparse
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--force-best-shift", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--decoys", type=int, default=N_PLACEBO,
                    help="decoys per feature; above the default, adds a swap test and writes _swapK outputs only")
    # 2026-11-23 sensitivity switches: change one setting and tag the outputs; defaults are unchanged
    ap.add_argument("--pit-ring", type=float, nargs=2, metavar=("IN", "OUT"))
    ap.add_argument("--pad-ring", type=float, nargs=2, metavar=("IN", "OUT"))
    ap.add_argument("--decoy-r", type=float, nargs=2, metavar=("MIN", "MAX"))
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="", help="extra output suffix for a sensitivity run")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    global PIT_RING, PAD_RING, DECOY_R
    if args.pit_ring:
        PIT_RING = tuple(args.pit_ring)
    if args.pad_ring:
        PAD_RING = tuple(args.pad_ring)
    if args.decoy_r:
        DECOY_R = tuple(args.decoy_r)
    force = args.force_best_shift
    n_decoys = args.decoys
    swap = n_decoys != N_PLACEBO
    sfx = ("_forcedshift" if force else "") + (f"_swap{n_decoys}" if swap else "") + (f"_{args.tag}" if args.tag else "")
    FIG.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    print(f"area {A.TAG}")
    idx, inten, tf, shape = load_stack()
    idx["season"] = idx.date.map(season_of)
    counts = idx.groupby(["track", "direction", "season"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
    print(counts)

    means = {}
    for (track, season), g in idx.groupby(["track", "season"]):
        for p, pi in (("hh", 0), ("hv", 1)):
            s = np.stack([inten[f][pi] for f in g.file])
            n_ok = np.isfinite(s).sum(0)
            # a pixel needs valid samples on at least half of the season's dates
            need = max(1, int(np.ceil(0.5 * len(g))))
            with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
                m = np.nanmean(s, axis=0)
            means[(track, season, p)] = np.where(n_ok >= need, m, np.nan)
    tracks = sorted(idx.track.unique())
    cover = canopy_cover(tf, shape)
    in_tile = np.isfinite(cover)

    # ---- registration per track ------------------------------------------------------
    reg, shift_of = [], {}
    for t in tracks:
        shift_of[t] = (0.0, 0.0)
        if (t, "leafon", "hv") not in means:
            continue
        hv = db(means[(t, "leafon", "hv")])
        res = {}
        for dx in SHIFTS:
            for dy in SHIFTS:
                c = cover if (dx, dy) == (0, 0) else canopy_cover(tf, shape, (dx, dy))
                ok = np.isfinite(c) & np.isfinite(hv)
                res[(dx, dy)] = float(spearmanr(c[ok], hv[ok]).statistic)
        (bx, by), br = max(res.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])
        r0 = res[(0, 0)]
        interior = abs(bx) < max(SHIFTS) and abs(by) < max(SHIFTS)
        use = force or (interior and br >= REG_MIN_RHO and br - r0 >= 0.02)
        if use:
            shift_of[t] = (float(bx), float(by))
        reg.append(dict(track=int(t), rho_unshifted=r0, best_dx=bx, best_dy=by, rho_best=br,
                        peak_inside_search=interior, applied=use))
        print(f"track {t}: rho0 {r0:.3f}, best {br:.3f} at ({bx:+d},{by:+d}) -> "
              f"{'applied' if use else 'as delivered'}")

    def aligned(arr, t):
        # a track pixel labelled x shows ground at x + shift; move it to that label
        cx, cy = int(round(shift_of[t][0] / 5)), int(round(shift_of[t][1] / 5))
        if cx == 0 and cy == 0:
            return arr
        outa = np.full_like(arr, np.nan)
        src_r0, dst_r0 = max(0, cy), max(0, -cy)
        src_c0, dst_c0 = max(0, -cx), max(0, cx)
        h, w = shape[0] - abs(cy), shape[1] - abs(cx)
        outa[dst_r0:dst_r0 + h, dst_c0:dst_c0 + w] = arr[src_r0:src_r0 + h, src_c0:src_c0 + w]
        return outa

    layers = {t: {f"{p}_{s}": aligned(means[(t, s, p)], t).ravel()
                  for s in SEASONS for p in ("hh", "hv") if (t, s, p) in means} for t in tracks}
    metrics = {}
    for p in ("hh", "hv"):
        for s in SEASONS:
            metrics[f"{p}_{s}"] = (f"{p}_{s}", None)
        metrics[f"{p}_change_leafon_vs_fall"] = (f"{p}_leafon", f"{p}_leafoff_fall")

    # ---- geometry ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    pads = read_layer(ANN, "plat").to_crs(CRS)[["pad_id", "geometry"]].dissolve(by="pad_id").reset_index()
    pits = read_layer(ANN, "pit_outside").to_crs(CRS).reset_index(drop=True)
    roads = read_layer(ANN, "roads").to_crs(CRS)
    feat_zone = rasterize([(g, 1) for g in pd.concat([pads.buffer(20), pits.buffer(20), roads.buffer(20)])],
                          out_shape=shape, transform=tf, fill=0, dtype="uint8").astype(bool)
    ok_flat = in_tile.ravel()
    bg_flat = (in_tile & ~feat_zone).ravel()
    pad_excl = pd.concat([pads.buffer(PAD_EXCL), roads.buffer(PAD_EXCL)]).union_all()
    pit_excl = pd.concat([pits.buffer(PIT_EXCL), roads.buffer(PIT_EXCL)]).union_all()

    # ---- positive control, per pixel ----------------------------------------------------
    control = []
    cov = cover.ravel()
    op, cl = bg_flat & (cov < 0.10), bg_flat & (cov > 0.90)
    for t in tracks:
        L = layers[t]
        for m, (num, den) in metrics.items():
            if num not in L or (den and den not in L):
                continue
            v = db(L[num]) - (db(L[den]) if den else 0.0)
            a, b = v[op & np.isfinite(v)], v[cl & np.isfinite(v)]
            a = rng.choice(a, min(20000, len(a)), replace=False)
            b = rng.choice(b, min(20000, len(b)), replace=False)
            control.append(dict(track=int(t), metric=m, open_median_db=float(np.median(a)),
                                closed_median_db=float(np.median(b)), auc_closed_gt_open=auc(b, a)))
    control = pd.DataFrame(control)
    print(control.round(3).to_string())
    # whole-tile shift between seasons: seasonal, or a beta-vs-provisional calibration offset
    tile_median_change = {}
    for t in tracks:
        for p in ("hh", "hv"):
            L = layers[t]
            if f"{p}_leafon" in L and f"{p}_leafoff_fall" in L:
                v = db(L[f"{p}_leafon"]) - db(L[f"{p}_leafoff_fall"])
                tile_median_change[(int(t), p)] = float(np.nanmedian(v[ok_flat]))
    print("tile median leaf-on minus leaf-off (dB):", tile_median_change)

    # ---- features and their decoys ---------------------------------------------------------
    results, per_feature = [], {}
    for kind, geoms, ids, excl, core_m, ring in (
            ("pad", pads.geometry, pads.pad_id, pad_excl, PAD_CORE_M, PAD_RING),
            ("pit", pits.geometry, pits.index, pit_excl, 0.0, PIT_RING)):
        rows, decoys_all = [], {m: [] for m in metrics}
        mats = {m: [] for m in metrics}
        for fid, g in zip(ids, geoms):
            core, rg = pixel_sets(g, core_m, ring, excl, tf, shape, ok_flat)
            if len(core) == 0 or len(rg) < 10:
                continue
            pls = placebo_sets(g, core_m, ring, excl, tf, shape, ok_flat, bg_flat, rng, n_decoys, tries=12 * n_decoys)
            if not pls:
                continue
            row = dict(id=fid, n_core=len(core), n_ring=len(rg), n_decoys=len(pls))
            for m, (num, den) in metrics.items():
                real = [set_value(core, rg, layers[t], num, den) for t in tracks]
                row[f"{m}_feature"] = np.nanmean(real) if np.isfinite(real).any() else np.nan
                pv = []
                for pc, pr in pls:
                    v = [set_value(pc, pr, layers[t], num, den) for t in tracks]
                    if np.isfinite(v).any():
                        pv.append(np.nanmean(v))
                row[f"{m}_decoy_median"] = float(np.median(pv)) if pv else np.nan
                decoys_all[m] += pv
                mats[m].append([row[f"{m}_feature"]] + pv)
            rows.append(row)
        df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
        per_feature[kind] = df
        print(f"{kind}: {len(df)} features with rings and decoys")
        if df.empty:
            continue
        for m in metrics:
            real = df[f"{m}_feature"].to_numpy()
            dec = df[f"{m}_decoy_median"].to_numpy()
            ok = np.isfinite(real) & np.isfinite(dec)
            if ok.sum() < 10:
                continue
            exc = real[ok] - dec[ok]
            sw = swap_test(mats[m], rng) if swap else None
            be = np.median(exc[rng.integers(0, ok.sum(), size=(B, ok.sum()))], axis=1)
            results.append(dict(features=kind, metric=m, n=int(ok.sum()),
                                median_feature_minus_ring_db=float(np.median(real[ok])),
                                median_decoy_minus_ring_db=float(np.median(dec[ok])),
                                median_excess_db=float(np.median(exc)),
                                excess_ci_lo=float(np.percentile(be, 2.5)),
                                excess_ci_hi=float(np.percentile(be, 97.5)),
                                auc_feature_gt_decoy=auc(real[ok], decoys_all[m]),
                                wilcoxon_p_excess=float(wilcoxon(exc).pvalue),
                                **({f"swap_{k}": v for k, v in sw.items()} if sw else {})))
    res = pd.DataFrame(results)
    print(res.round(3).to_string())

    # ---- outputs ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    prof = dict(driver="GTiff", height=shape[0], width=shape[1], count=1, dtype="float32",
                crs=CRS, transform=tf, nodata=np.nan, compress="deflate")
    n_written = 0
    for t in ([] if force or swap or args.tag else tracks):   # sensitivity runs do not overwrite the rasters
        d = idx[idx.track == t].direction.iat[0]
        # rasters stay as delivered even when the statistics use a lidar shift
        tag = "asdelivered"
        R = {f"{p}_{s}": means[(t, s, p)].ravel() for s in SEASONS for p in ("hh", "hv") if (t, s, p) in means}
        for m, (num, den) in metrics.items():
            if num not in R or (den and den not in R):
                continue
            v = (db(R[num]) - (db(R[den]) if den else 0.0)).reshape(shape)
            with rasterio.open(SRC / raster_name(m, t, d, tag), "w", **prof) as dst:
                dst.write(v.astype(np.float32), 1)
            n_written += 1
    print(f"wrote {n_written} rasters to {SRC}")
    for kind, df in per_feature.items():
        df.to_csv(OUT / f"nisar_gslc_stack_{kind}_vs_ring_and_decoys_per_feature{sfx}_{A.TAG}_5m.csv", index=False)
    res.to_csv(OUT / f"nisar_gslc_stack_pad_pit_vs_decoy_summary_by_season{sfx}_{A.TAG}_5m.csv", index=False)
    control.to_csv(OUT / f"nisar_gslc_stack_open_vs_closed_canopy_control_by_track{sfx}_{A.TAG}_5m.csv", index=False)
    (OUT / f"nisar_gslc_stack_pad_pit_vs_decoy_summary_by_season{sfx}_{A.TAG}_5m.json").write_text(json.dumps(dict(
        n_dates_by_track_season=counts.stack().rename("n").reset_index().to_dict("records"),
        registration=reg, shift_applied_m={int(k): v for k, v in shift_of.items()},
        seasons=SEASONS, n_decoys=N_PLACEBO,
        tile_median_change_leafon_minus_fall_db={f"{k[0]}_{k[1]}": v for k, v in tile_median_change.items()}, control=control.to_dict("records"),
        results=results), indent=1, default=str))

    # ---- figure ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # map the track with the most leaf-off dates; one-date seasons are pure speckle
    # (among tracks that have a leaf-on mean; 613590 has a track without one)
    t0 = max([t for t in tracks if "hh_leafon" in layers[t]],
             key=lambda t: counts.xs(t, level="track")["leafoff_fall"].sum())
    d0 = idx[idx.track == t0].direction.iat[0]
    L = layers[t0]
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
    import _nisar_fig_style as S
    S.apply()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(7.2, 6.4), gridspec_kw=dict(height_ratios=[1, 0.9]))
    ext = (tf.c, tf.c + shape[1] * 5, tf.f - shape[0] * 5, tf.f)
    img = db(L["hh_leafon"]).reshape(shape)
    lo, hi = np.nanpercentile(img[in_tile], [2, 98])
    ax[0, 0].imshow(img, extent=ext, cmap="gray", vmin=lo, vmax=hi, interpolation="nearest")
    pads.boundary.plot(ax=ax[0, 0], color=FEAT_C, lw=0.5)
    n_on = int(counts.loc[(t0, d0), "leafon"])
    S.panel(ax[0, 0], "a", f"HH, summer mean ({n_on} dates), track {t0}{d0}. Pads outlined")
    ch = (db(L["hv_leafon"]) - db(L["hv_leafoff_fall"])).reshape(shape)
    ch = ch - tile_median_change[(int(t0), "hv")]
    im = ax[0, 1].imshow(ch, extent=ext, cmap="PuOr", vmin=-4, vmax=4, interpolation="nearest")
    pads.boundary.plot(ax=ax[0, 1], color=INK, lw=0.4)
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax[0, 1], fraction=0.046, pad=0.02).set_label("HV summer minus fall,\nrelative to tile median (dB)")
    S.panel(ax[0, 1], "b", f"HV summer minus fall, track {t0}{d0}")
    for a in ax[0]:
        S.map_axes(a)
        a.set_xlim(ext[0] + 200, ext[1] - 200); a.set_ylim(ext[2] + 200, ext[3] - 200)

    shown = ["hh_leafon", "hv_leafon", "hh_leafoff_fall", "hv_leafoff_fall",
             "hh_change_leafon_vs_fall", "hv_change_leafon_vs_fall"]
    label = {"leafon": "summer", "leafoff_fall": "fall", "change_leafon_vs_fall": "summer\n− fall"}

    def panel(a, letter, kind, title):
        df = per_feature[kind]
        if df.empty:
            a.text(0.5, 0.5, f"no annotated {kind}s in {A.TAG}", ha="center", va="center", transform=a.transAxes)
            a.set_axis_off()
            return
        for i, m in enumerate(shown):
            for off, col, mk, vals in ((-0.18, FEAT_C, "o", df[f"{m}_feature"]),
                                       (0.18, RING_C, "s", df[f"{m}_decoy_median"])):
                v = vals.dropna().to_numpy()
                a.scatter(i + off + rng.uniform(-0.1, 0.1, len(v)), v, s=1.5, color=col, marker=mk,
                          alpha=0.25, lw=0)
                q = np.percentile(v, [25, 50, 75])
                a.errorbar(i + off, q[1], yerr=[[q[1] - q[0]], [q[2] - q[1]]], fmt=mk, color=INK,
                           mfc=col, ms=4.5, capsize=2.5, elinewidth=0.8, mew=0.6)
        a.axhline(0, color=S.GREY, ls="--", lw=0.6)
        a.set_xticks(range(len(shown)))
        a.set_xticklabels([m[:2].upper() + "\n" + label[m[3:]] for m in shown], fontsize=8)
        a.set_ylabel("Feature minus its ring (dB)")
        a.set_ylim(-3, 3)
        S.panel(a, letter, title)
        a.scatter([], [], color=FEAT_C, marker="o", label=f"Mapped {kind}s")
        a.scatter([], [], color=RING_C, marker="s", label="Control spots")
        a.legend(loc="lower left")

    panel(ax[1, 0], "c", "pad", f"Pads (n = {len(per_feature['pad'])}), 20–60 m ring")
    panel(ax[1, 1], "d", "pit", f"Pits (n = {len(per_feature['pit'])}), 10–30 m ring")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fp = FIG / f"nisar_gslc_stack_pad_pit_vs_decoy_leafon_leafoff_seasonal_change{sfx}_{A.TAG}_5m.png"
    fig.savefig(fp, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    print(f"wrote {fp}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
